line: Then, far away in the waking world, a man reads her name from a stolen book.
His men carry off her three treasures: her helm, her pouch of sand, and her ruby.
Hours later, his followers have gone home. Burgess comes back down, alone.
Alex remembers the night his father came up from the cellar white as chalk, and took down every mirror in the house.
Burgess sends him to bed. Then he takes down every mirror in the house.
Burgess climbs the cellar stairs very slowly, and locks the door behind him, twice.
Upstairs, his small son Alex is sitting on the top step in his pyjamas. He has heard everything.
Aurie calls them, and they come.
Choronzon's form swallows hers. The arena howls with delight.
Only Lucifer remains, alone on his throne, as if he has been waiting for her.
He has sent every demon and every damned soul out into the dark. All that is left is the key, and he is giving it to her.
Aurie cuts. The wings fall away into a storm of feathers.
Azazel shrieks. The jar cracks, and Nada's soul spills free into Aurie's hands.
Nada strikes her across the face, and walks into the light alone.
Nada refuses every gift, and leaves without a word.
Faerie's Hell is a strange, dancing place. Nobody is sure what it is for.
Somewhere in the waking world, a man with no wings plays piano in a bar, and thinks of her kindly.
The lock turns to sand in Aurie's hand. The door swings open.
He sees a pale woman in black standing in a room he locked. He understands at once who she has come for.
Only a small white skull is left on the carpet. Where its eyes should be, two tiny rows of teeth.
The Corinthian's skull sits on a shelf in Lucienne's library.
She dreams. And the walls between the dreams of everyone in the house come down.
Aurie raises her hand. Rose does not run. She only closes her eyes.
Rose Walker is alive. Unity Kincaid sleeps at last, for good.
Matthew dives, screaming, straight at Loki's eyes.
Loki drops the child and is gone. Daniel is safe. Daniel is safe.
Daniel sleeps in the library, among the books, and does not cry once.
Lyta does not wait for Aurie. She walks straight into the fire's light, and takes her son out of a god's hands.
Loki looks at the two of them, and decides he has somewhere else to be.
The lantern goes out.
Aurie breaks the old law, and every faerie in the glade turns away from her.
On the walls, the sigils of her family glow like doors. Desire's is laughing. Delirium's is weeping. Destruction's is open.
And somewhere in the Dreaming, in the library, a small boy opens his eyes, and they are full of stars.
Lucienne is not there. Her lantern is, on an empty chair.
Calliope, who came to forgive, and did.
Johanna Constantine, smoking at the back, who will deny that she came.
Matthew, who will not stop saying boss.
Nuala of Faerie, holding a single white flower.
And from Fiddler's Green, a whole meadow of wildflowers, which walked there by itself.
Lyta Hall stands at the back, holding her son's hand, and does not look away.
Delirium, who remembers that her sister came to find her once, on a desert road, and said sorry.
Delirium, who leaves a little fish made of gold light on the bier, and tells it a secret.
Delirium comes looking for her, years later, and finds only ruins and a door that will not open.
In a locked house in Florida, a little boy named Jed is dreaming of his sister. The Corinthian has heard him.
Rose finds her brother first. By one night. She will never know how close it was.
A young man on a bridge, who did not mean to fall. Death holds his hand all the way down, and he is not afraid.
She walks past the sleeping poor on the steps of churches, and gives each of them one warm dream. It costs her nothing. She does it anyway.
At the river she stops, and stands until the lamps go out.
Behind her, in the fog, a drunk man is still sitting in a tavern with two glasses, refusing to go home.
That night, everyone at the wake falls asleep at the same moment, and dreams the same dream.
Hob Gadling comes to the White Horse every year now, on the same day, and buys two pints.
It is about an island, and a magician who rules it, and who at the very end breaks his staff, and drowns his book, and gives his power away.
Pride is a door that locks from the inside.
He paints her portrait. It is a very bad painting. She keeps it.
A raven sleeps on the back of Aurie's throne.
A raven lands on a stone beside her. Boss? Matthew asks. Are you all right?
Lucienne comes down from the library with a lantern, and waits beside her, saying nothing.
Delirium has gone somewhere inside herself, and her body sits in the car like an empty coat.
Behind her, Paul begins to sing, very softly, to keep Alex company in the waking.
Lucienne brings her the day's dreams. Aurie listens to none of them.
Rose does not thank her. But that night, and every night after, she dreams of her brother laughing in the sun.
And she remembers an old woman in a blue dressing gown, who took her place.
In 1927 an old writer trapped her and kept her in his house. When he died, a young novelist bought her.
Calliope prayed to the Three. The Three told her: Dream is free again. Call to her.
Despair's realm is grey, and full of mirrors. In every one, someone is looking at the worst thing they have ever done.
Your helm, your sand and your ruby are out there, scattered across the waking world.
Next, the helm. A demon has it, in Hell.
Behind the counter, Bette the waitress is still asleep, smiling. Dee walked past her a hundred times, and never once saw her.
Bette the waitress dreams she is writing stories, and every one of them has a happy ending.
She sleeps on, inside the seaside dream you gave her.
Her dream stays grey for a long, long time.
A woman is waiting under a porch, as if she has been expecting trouble.
Lyta's grief has nowhere to go. Thessaly takes her somewhere far away, and teaches her to live with it.
Lyta keeps her son. He grows up ordinary, and loved, and dreams very vividly.
